Recommended protocol, synthesized from the documentation: freeze a per-category manifest containing SHA-256 hashes of the selected checkpoint, generated predictor, architecture/configuration, ordered item mapping, fixtures and dependency versions; record seeds, device, dtype and backend settings. Explicitly reload that checkpoint into the live reference with strict state loading; compare every parameter/buffer and mapping against the exported model. Use evaluation mode and inference mode. A checkpoint filename alone does not establish identity. [PyTorch loading guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html).

Run the actual exported public entry point through a fresh interpreter using `sys.executable`, explicit working directory/environment, `check=True`, captured logs and a finite timeout, for example 120 seconds. If the interface is callable, a minimal child runner should import the generated file and invoke its public function. Run reference and export sequentially on the same single visible GPU, terminating each process before starting the next. Feed identical raw histories and ordered candidates across all four routes, covering short, truncated and padded histories. Observe actual model inputs through non-mutating hooks; never substitute preprocessing. Assert exact token/candidate IDs, left padding and appended BERT mask/readout placement. Timeouts, missing artifacts and nonzero exits fail the audit. [Python subprocess](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html).

Preserve scores in binary tensors/arrays; if decimal serialization is required, use round-trip precision: 9 significant digits for FP32, 17 for FP64. Require identical shapes/order and finite scores before testing `abs(export-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference)`. Proposed initial `(rtol, atol)`: FP64 `(1e-7,1e-9)`, FP32 `(1e-5,1e-6)`, FP16 `(1e-3,1e-3)`, BF16 `(1e-2,1e-2)`; calibrate and freeze thresholds before acceptance, since these are not universal guarantees. Report maximum errors and ranking disagreements separately. [NumPy comparison semantics](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.allclose), [PyTorch numerical limits](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).
